gh issue comment 162 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
One refinement to the "visible in shipped output too" evidence, measured
today on this branch's build (plain mode, no `-t`, in a 100x30 tmux pane):

The end-of-game pair only runs together when the answer arrives before
the prompt does. With the player waiting for the question, the terminal's
own echo of the Enter ends the line and the display is fine:

```
Do you want your score recorded?n
Do you want to play again?
```

Send the `n` ahead of the prompt -- typeahead, or any piped stdin, which
is how `tests/golden.sh` and the scripted plain-mode journey in AGENTS.md
see it -- and the echo lands somewhere earlier, so the two questions
concatenate exactly as the issue shows:

```
Do you want your score recorded?Do you want to play again?
```

So the shipped-output symptom is real but conditional: it is the echo
that has been ending those lines, not the game. That makes it worse for
the recordings and the test journeys than for a player at a normal pace,
and it means a change that stops relying on the echo cannot be validated
by watching an interactive session.

Found while checking a `ui-review` observation on the branch for #174
(the notice running into the play-again prompt at the retry), which turns
out to be the same conditional shape rather than a separate defect.
EOF
)"

```
100x30 pane, env LINES=40 COLUMNS=190
  Terminal is 100x30 but LINES/COLUMNS make it 190x40.
  Grow to 190x40, or unset LINES and COLUMNS and rerun sst -t.
```

That matters more than an ordinary gap because the comment at `sst.c:506-520` builds its 61-column bound on exactly this case being reachable ("The 17 needs both axes named... so both are then oversize"). It is also the longest line the branch can emit, so it is the one at risk against the 72-column budget. I verified it by hand and it is correct — 61 columns on a 72-column window, unwrapped, eleven to spare — but no test would catch a regression in it. `tests/tui.sh:2993` greps `Unset LINES and COLUMNS`, which is the *non*-growable form and a different branch.

**The floor clamp in `tui_refusal_growable()` is unreachable from its only caller,** so no test can cover it through the game. `sst.c` calls it only where `smallwindow` is false, which forces `termrows >= MINROWS` and `termcols >= MINCOLS`; both `needrows` and `needcols` are then already at or above the floor, so `*rows = needrows < MINROWS ? MINROWS : needrows` and its width twin never fire. The comment at `tui.c:1275-1280` says as much ("so the answer stands on its own for a caller that has not checked the window is over it"), so this is deliberate defensive code, not a gap to fill — reporting it so the resolution is on the record rather than implied.

input.command:
gh issue create --title "Eleven CRLF source files are unprotected by .gitattributes, and a whole-file flip is invisible to every check" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Eleven tracked files are entirely CRLF, and every one of them is a file
the build compiles or the game reads:

```
ai.c  battle.c  events.c  finish.c  moving.c  planets.c
reports.c  setup.c  sst.c  sst.h  sst.doc
```

(Measured with `grep -c $'\r'` against the line count: all lines, not
some.) The newer files -- `tui.c`, `tui.h`, `tuifmt.c`, `rules.c`,
`rules.h`, `osx.c`, `osx.h` -- are LF, so the tree is mixed by vintage.

`.gitattributes` covers only `tests/golden/*.txt`:

```
# The golden fixtures are compared byte for byte, so a clone that
# rewrote their line endings would fail every journey.
tests/golden/*.txt -text
```

The reasoning in that comment applies to the eleven as well, and stops
one directory short of them.

## Why it matters

A wholesale line-ending flip in any of those files passes every check
this repository has. The compiler does not care: I flipped all 1130
lines of `sst.c` to LF by accident and the `verifier` rebuilt both
`ci-*` presets and compared disassembly -- `.text` byte-identical in
Debug and Release, zero warnings under `-Werror`. `ctest` passes, the
journeys pass, the golden recordings pass, `analyze` passes. The only
thing that shows it is `git diff --stat`, where `sst.c` read 2314
changed lines instead of 58.

Two ways it gets in:

- **A clone that normalizes.** With no `text` attribute git falls back
  to `core.autocrlf`, which is `true` by default in Git for Windows.
  Checked out and committed back, all eleven files flip -- about 8,700
  lines across a diff nobody can review.
- **An editing tool in text mode.** Python's `open(p).read()` /
  `open(p, "w").write()` strips CRLF silently, and so does any editor
  configured to normalize on save. This is how it happened here, on the
  branch for #174; it was caught by reading `git diff --stat` and not
  by anything automatic.

Either way the damage is a diff that looks like a rewrite, or -- worse
-- a real change buried in one, since the genuine hunks are
indistinguishable from the noise once the whole file has moved.

## Where it was found

While preparing the branch for #174 (the oversize-pin refusal notice).
Two comment edits to `sst.c` made with a text-mode script stripped the
file's line endings; the `verifier` had flagged only that `sst.c` was
edited mid-run, and its `.text` comparison correctly reported the
binaries identical, which is exactly why nothing else noticed.

## Fixing it

Add the eleven to `.gitattributes` with their actual ending, so git
stops guessing and a clone on any platform gets them back byte for
byte. Something like:

```
*.c  -text
*.h  -text
sst.doc -text
```

-- except that `-text` on `*.c` would also freeze the LF files, which
is the right outcome but should be stated deliberately rather than
inherited. Per-file `eol=crlf` for the eleven is the narrower option.

Worth deciding at the same time whether a check belongs in CI. A
`git diff --check`-style guard, or a test that asserts each of the
eleven still has no bare LF, would turn the silent case into a failing
one. That is the part the golden-fixture line above does not have
either.
EOF
)"

## Verdict: **approve**

Approval covers the exact state I reviewed: branch `fix/oversize-pin-notice` at `HEAD = 6f538a9` with nothing staged, nothing untracked, and six modified files — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c`, `tui.h`, `sst.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `README.md`, `sst.doc` (`git diff main` is the whole change). The three findings below are comment-only; if you fix any of them the reviewed state changes and step 11 asks for a fresh (cheap) round.

---

## Findings

### should-fix

**`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c:487`** — the sentence now contradicts the paragraph 19 lines below it.

`The three that carry numbers get no column count here.` is followed, in the same comment block, by `The grow-or-unset line added for #174 is the third, and it does get a count ... 61 columns`. Everything in the paragraph the first sentence introduces (the "five attempts were wrong" reasoning, the fifteen-columns-inside result, the "under 72 it cannot pass 52" result) is about the size report and the retry line only — the two. A reader takes the opening sentence as spec, and it is false for the third line.

Failure scenario: the next person to touch this line reads "no column count here", believes there is no stated bound to keep true, and changes the wording past 61 columns without re-deriving anything.

Suggested fix: restore `The two that carry numbers get no column count here.` (the size report and the retry line) and let the following paragraph introduce the third as the one that *can* be bounded — or reword to `Three lines carry numbers. Two of them get no column count here:`.

### nit

**`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c:510`** — `tui_refusal_growable() prints nothing where an axis is under the floor` makes the function the subject of "prints"; it prints nothing under any circumstances, it returns `FALSE`. Suggest `answers FALSE where an axis is under the floor`, which is also what makes the "so both are then oversize" step follow.

**`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:1195-1232`** — the 38-line doc block headed `Whether a pinned dimension is what refused the player, and which.` now sits immediately above `oversize()` rather than above `blames()`, which is what it describes; only its last paragraph (1227-1232) is about the split. A reader arriving at `oversize()` gets a header that is not about it. Suggest moving the "The two halves are named…" paragraph to its own short header above `oversize()`/`underfloor()` and keeping the rest attached to `blames()`.

---

## Review coverage (`ui-review`)

The diff plainly reaches the player, and the pass ran twice with a coverage list that names journeys the change actually reaches (the four advice forms and the 61-column both-axes line). I agree with your judgment that the post-round-2 edits did not need a third round, and I checked it rather than took it: the only player-visible strings the diff introduces or alters are the four `proutf`/`prout` advice lines and the two size-report lines in `refusal_notice()`, and I drove all six live (see below) — they are byte-identical to the text quoted in the manuals and in your round-2 account. The manual edits made after round 2 are not player-visible in-game: the block you changed sits under "Modifications I made:" at `sst.doc:1562`, which is not a help topic, and `README.md` is not read by the game at all.

Limit on that: I can only compare the final state against your description of what round 2 saw. The intermediate states are not in git, so "no printed line changed after round 2" is verified as far as the final artefact allows and no further.

---

## What I verified independently

- **CRLF integrity** (you asked me to check this rather than take your word). Per file, working tree vs `HEAD`: `sst.c` 1184/1184 lines CR-terminated (HEAD 1130/1130), `sst.doc` 1714/1714 (HEAD 1709/1709), and `README.md`, `tests/tui.sh`, `tui.c`, `tui.h` contain zero CR bytes anywhere. No mixed lines, no missing final newline, every file matches HEAD's convention. (`git diff --check` flags the CRLF files as "trailing whitespace" — that is the CR, and it does the same on HEAD, so it is not a finding.)
- **Build**: `gcc -std=gnu17 -DSCORE -DCAPTURE -DCLOAKING -Wall -Wextra -Wmissing-prototypes -Werror -O2` on `tui.c` and `sst.c` — clean, including `-Wmaybe-uninitialized` over the `needcols`/`needrows` pair, which are only read under the short-circuited `blame != NULL && tui_refusal_growable(...)`.
- **The 512 clamp** the 61-column bound rests on: `COLUMNS=99999 tput cols` → 512, `COLUMNS=513` → 512, `COLUMNS=511` → 511. And the worst case end-to-end, at 72x24 with both pinned to 99999: the game printed `Grow to 512x512, or unset LINES and COLUMNS and rerun sst -t.` at exactly 61 columns, eleven inside the window. The 38-char fixed text, the 59/82 figures for the rejected "for panels next game" wording, and the "75 unclamped" figure (two 10-digit `int`-max pins, which is what `pinned()` admits) all recompute correctly.
- **`tui_refusal_growable()` against `tui_init()`'s gate**, by hand over every shape and live under tmux on a private socket (`-L crev`, `-f /dev/null`, killed after): the per-axis max is right where the pinned pair is wrong (`LINES=40 COLUMNS=80` at 100x30 reports `make it 80x40` and correctly advises `Grow to 100x40`), the under-the-floor veto fires on the mixed shape (`LINES=40 COLUMNS=60` → unset-only), and both `MINROWS`/`MINCOLS` clamps are genuinely unreachable from `sst.c`'s `!smallwindow` caller, as your `tui.c` comment states. I also confirmed the offered size is actually *accepted*: `LINES=40 COLUMNS=80` in a 100x40 window brings the panels up with no notice.
- **Every literal in `tests/tui.sh`** — the three new arms, the rewritten "oversize LINES" arm and the two `scrollback_count` retry literals — matched against live game output character for character, including the retry sizes (150x30 with `COLUMNS=190` and 100x35 with `LINES=40` print exactly the strings those arms count, and identically to their startup notices, so the `-lt 2` counts still mean what they say). The three surviving old arms (`undersize pin`, `pin equal to the window`, the 3609 compound check) still take the branches their comments claim.
- Line widths: the new `sst.doc` block wraps at ≤69, matching the surrounding text; `tui.h`'s new entry matches `tui_refused_sizes`'s layout exactly.

## What I could not review

- The full `ctest` battery, both `ci-*` presets, the golden recordings and the complete `tests/tui.sh` run — the `verifier`'s scope, and it reports both configurations clean. I did not re-run them.
- The intermediate worktree states the two `ui-review` rounds saw, as above.
- Your mutation proofs, which ran on copies outside the repository; the two breaks you name (`needcols = refusedtermcols` unconditionally, and dropping the under-the-floor test) do map onto arms that would catch them — the "both axes oversize" and "pinned axis" arms for the first, "oversize height with an undersize width" for the second — which is consistent with what you reported.

## Verdict: **approve**

Approval covers the exact state I reviewed: branch `fix/oversize-pin-notice` at `HEAD = 6f538a9` with nothing staged, nothing untracked, and six modified files — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c`, `tui.h`, `sst.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `README.md`, `sst.doc` (`git diff main` is the whole change). ---

## Findings

### should-fix

**`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c:487`** — the sentence now contradicts the paragraph 19 lines below it.

`The three that carry numbers get no column count here.` is followed, in the same comment block, by `The grow-or-unset line added for #174 is the third, and it does get a count ... 61 columns`. Everything in the paragraph the first sentence introduces (the "five attempts were wrong" reasoning, the fifteen-columns-inside result, the "under 72 it cannot pass 52" result) is about the size report and the retry line only — the two. A reader takes the opening sentence as spec, and it is false for the third line.

Failure scenario: the next person to touch this line reads "no column count here", believes there is no stated bound to keep true, and changes the wording past 61 columns without re-deriving anything.

Suggested fix: restore `The two that carry numbers get no column count here.` (the size report and the retry line) and let the following paragraph introduce the third as the one that *can* be bounded — or reword to `Three lines carry numbers. Two of them get no column count here:`.

### nit

**`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c:510`** — `tui_refusal_growable() prints nothing where an axis is under the floor` makes the function the subject of "prints"; it prints nothing under any circumstances, it returns `FALSE`. Suggest `answers FALSE where an axis is under the floor`, which is also what makes the "so both are then oversize" step follow.

**`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:1195-1232`** — the 38-line doc block headed `Whether a pinned dimension is what refused the player, and which.` now sits immediately above `oversize()` rather than above `blames()`, which is what it describes; only its last paragraph (1227-1232) is about the split. A reader arriving at `oversize()` gets a header that is not about it. Suggest moving the "The two halves are named…" paragraph to its own short header above `oversize()`/`underfloor()` and keeping the rest attached to `blames()`.

---

## Review coverage (`ui-review`)

The diff plainly reaches the player, and the pass ran twice with a coverage list that names journeys the change actually reaches (the four advice forms and the 61-column both-axes line). I agree with your judgment that the post-round-2 edits did not need a third round, and I checked it rather than took it: the only player-visible strings the diff introduces or alters are the four `proutf`/`prout` advice lines and the two size-report lines in `refusal_notice()`, and I drove all six live (see below) — they are byte-identical to the text quoted in the manuals and in your round-2 account. The manual edits made after round 2 are not player-visible in-game: the block you changed sits under "Modifications I made:" at `sst.doc:1562`, which is not a help topic, and `README.md` is not read by the game at all.

Limit on that: I can only compare the final state against your description of what round 2 saw. The intermediate states are not in git, so "no printed line changed after round 2" is verified as far as the final artefact allows and no further.

---

## What I verified independently

- **CRLF integrity** (you asked me to check this rather than take your word). Per file, working tree vs `HEAD`: `sst.c` 1184/1184 lines CR-terminated (HEAD 1130/1130), `sst.doc` 1714/1714 (HEAD 1709/1709), and `README.md`, `tests/tui.sh`, `tui.c`, `tui.h` contain zero CR bytes anywhere. - **Build**: `gcc -std=gnu17 -DSCORE -DCAPTURE -DCLOAKING -Wall -Wextra -Wmissing-prototypes -Werror -O2` on `tui.c` and `sst.c` — clean, including `-Wmaybe-uninitialized` over the `needcols`/`needrows` pair, which are only read under the short-circuited `blame != NULL && tui_refusal_growable(...)`.

title:	The tui test's timeout comment says ~11s; it takes about a minute
state:	OPEN
author:	scottdensmore (Scott Densmore)
labels:	
comments:	2
assignees:	
projects:	
milestone:	
issue-type:	
parent:	
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	
blocking:	
number:	101
--
## Problem

`CMakeLists.txt` sets a 300-second timeout on the `tui` test and
explains it with:

> The timeout is far above the ~11s it takes to pass

Measured: **51s** on `main`, and **68s** after #88 adds squeeze cases.
The claim is out by roughly six times, and every branch that adds a

# Verdict: approve

Reviewed state: branch `fix/oversize-pin-notice` at HEAD `6f538a9` with six modified, unstaged files (`README.md`, `sst.c`, `sst.doc`, `tests/tui.sh`, `tui.c`, `tui.h`; +344/−30; working-diff sha1 `91ae6a197154`). No staged changes, no untracked files. Approval is valid only for this exact state.

## What I verified independently (not taken on your word)

**Line endings.** `sst.c` is 1185 lines, 1185 CRLF, 1185 CR total, zero lone CRs, final byte pair `\r\n`; `sst.doc` likewise (1714/1714). `tui.c`, `tui.h`, `tests/tui.sh`, `README.md` are wholly LF. The `git diff main` hunks for `sst.c` are only the intended ones — a whole-file EOL flip would have rewritten every line — so the restoration is complete. The `git diff --check` "trailing whitespace" noise on `sst.c`/`sst.doc` is just the CR in a CRLF file and is pre-existing, not introduced.

**The printed lines, live.** Drove `build/ci-debug/sst` (built 12:22, newer than both changed C files) under tmux on my own socket (`-L rvw`, `-f /dev/null`), 100x30:

- `COLUMNS=190` → `Grow to 190x30, or unset COLUMNS and rerun sst -t.`
- `LINES=40 COLUMNS=80` → `Grow to 100x40, or unset LINES and rerun sst -t.` (the larger-per-axis rule, not the report's `80x40`)
- `LINES=40 COLUMNS=190` → `Grow to 190x40, or unset LINES and COLUMNS and rerun sst -t.` (60 columns)
- `LINES=40 COLUMNS=60` → `Unset LINES and COLUMNS, rerun sst -t -- classic for now.` (unset-only preserved under a floor-blamed axis)
- `LINES=99999 COLUMNS=99999` → `Grow to 512x512, or unset LINES and COLUMNS and rerun sst -t.` — exactly the 61 columns `sst.c:508` claims, and the worst case is reachable.

Every one matches the `fallback` arm strings and both manuals byte for byte.

**The 512 clamp the 61-column bound rests on.** Built a standalone ncurses probe (`initscr()`, print `LINES`/`COLS`) against the system ncurses 6.6.20251231 and ran it on a pty with `LINES=99999 COLUMNS=99999`: `LINES=512 COLS=512`. The three-digit premise holds, and the fixed-text arithmetic checks out (38 fixed + 17 blame + 3 + 3 = 61; the rejected "for panels next game" variant is 59 fixed → 82, as stated).

**"Meeting the pin" end to end.** Reproduced the arm by hand: refused at 100x30 with `COLUMNS=190`, `quit`/`n` to the play-again prompt, `resize-window -x 190 -y 30`, `y` — panels up in the same process, and `capture-pane -p -S -` returned **1** occurrence of `LINES/COLUMNS make it`. So your correction of the earlier version is right on both counts: counting the advice line would indeed pass with the panels down (a de-blamed pin prints the report alone), and tmux does keep the pre-alternate history — `screen_alternate_on()` copies the visible rows into `saved_grid` and clears on the *same* grid, so the scrollback survives. The comment at `tests/tui.sh:3814-3823` is correct and does not contradict the older note at `tests/tui.sh:134-137`, which is about content written *while* on the alt screen.

**Whole file green.** `tests/tui.sh build/ci-ebug/sst Debug` — sorry, `tests/tui.sh build/ci-debug/sst Debug` — exits 0, `tui OK`, zero FAIL lines, in this exact worktree. `sh -n` and `shellcheck -s sh` clean. `gcc -std=gnu17 -O2 -DSCORE -DCAPTURE -DCLOAKING -Wall -Wextra -Wmissing-prototypes -Werror -c` on both `sst.c` and `tui.c` is clean, so the uninitialized `needcols`/`needrows` on the FALSE path draws no `-Wmaybe-uninitialized` at optimisation.

**The logic, case by case.** `tui_refusal_growable()`'s offered size is exactly sufficient in every reachable shape: the oversize axis's pin is ≥ the floor (else `underfloor` would have returned FALSE), and the non-oversize axis is either a tolerated pin ≤ the window or the window itself. The two floor clamps also produce a correct answer for the hypothetical smallwindow caller (70x20 with `COLUMNS=75` → 75x24, which really is accepted). `oversize()` implies pinned, since `tui_init()` `resize_term()`s a free axis to the ioctl's value and `term_v != 0` implies `haveterm`.

## Findings

**Nit — `tui.h:85-90`:** the header says growable answers "FALSE where no window is big enough", which is untrue of the ordinary too-small terminal. At 70x20 with nothing exported, neither axis is oversize, so the function returns FALSE — yet growing the window to 72x24 is precisely what works. The body's doc block is pin-scoped and accurate; the header is the one-line contract a future caller reads, and the block at `tui.c:1283-1292` explicitly contemplates one (the `smallwindow` branch "were it ever to want a size"), which is the caller that would be misled. Suggested fix: "FALSE where no oversize pin is to blame — including the plain too-small terminal, where growing does help — and the two outputs are then unset."

Nothing at blocker or should-fix severity.

## The two resolutions you flagged

I do not dispute either.

- **No LINES-axis "meeting the pin" arm.** Agreed. `tui_init()`'s oversize gate is `LINES > winsz.ws_row || COLS > winsz.ws_col` — one expression over both axes — and the retry site in `sst.c:689-693` is axis-blind; the axis-specific code (`pinned("LINES")` in `resize_term()` and in `axis_moved()`) is already reached by "pinned height", "pinned height unchanged" and "env size". A second full-game journey would re-prove a shared gate at real cost against a timeout already at 62%.
- **The `tui` timing note belonging to `CMakeLists.txt` and going to #101.** Correct under step 9: it is about code this diff does not touch, and filing is the answer there.

## The post-verifier edit

I accept it without another verifier round, and for a stronger reason than "it's only a comment": the edit is inside an `elif` chain where a misplaced comment would be a syntax error, and `sh -n` plus `shellcheck -s sh` both come back clean here, and I ran the whole file green against a binary built from the current sources. The verifier's earlier Debug *and* Release passes covered the arm's executable content unchanged.

## Review coverage

`ui-review` was owed — the diff adds a line the game prints — and you report two bound rounds with the current player-visible strings byte-identical to what round 2 exercised (the four advice forms and the size reports). I checked what I could: the diff's entire player-visible surface is those `proutf`/`prout` strings, all of which I reproduced live above, and the manual edits made after that round cannot reach a player *in game* — `helpme()` (`sst.c:169-200`) starts at a `  Mnemonic:` line and stops at the first line containing `******`, and the last such line before the changed block is `sst.doc:1471` (`********MODIFICATIONS********`), with no `Mnemonic:` entry after it. So the changed manual text is unreachable by `help`, and no fresh `ui-review` is owed for it.

## What I could not review

- The `ui-review` and `verifier` sessions themselves — I have only your account of their verdicts and coverage. My check is the one above: the strings they say they exercised are the strings the game prints today.
- The mutation proofs (`|| (pinned("COLUMNS") && COLS == winsz.ws_col)`, the `refusedtermcols` substitution, the dropped under-the-floor test). I did not re-run them. I did confirm each named arm exists and would in fact be the arm that breaks: "one pinned" runs `COLUMNS=80` in an 80-column pane, so the exact-match break takes its `want_quadtitle` down; the `needcols`→`refusedtermcols` break turns "both axes oversize" into `Grow to 100x40` and moves the "pinned axis" retry's 190; and dropping the floor test turns "oversize height with an undersize width" into `Grow to 100x40`, which I confirmed is wrong advice by running that env myself.
- macOS: the 512 clamp is measured on this machine's ncurses 6.6 only, and the 61-column bound is stated as resting on it. Only a nine-digit pin on both axes could exceed 72 without the clamp, so I am not raising it.

| 100x30 | `LINES=40 COLUMNS=60` | `Unset LINES and COLUMNS, rerun sst -t -- classic for now.` |
| 72x24 | `LINES=99999 COLUMNS=99999` | `Grow to 512x512, or unset LINES and COLUMNS and rerun sst -t.` (61 columns, no wrap) |

Those match the manuals' quoted strings character for character, and the third confirms the load-bearing claim the "oversize height under a tolerated width" arm exists for: the advice's `100x40` is not the report's `80x40`.
